definition: Linagora is a French open source software editor, founded in June 2000 by Alexandre Zapolsky and Michel-Marie Maudet.
details: Located in France, as well as in Belgium, Canada, Vietnam, the United States and Tunisia, the company employs around 200 people. In 2023, Linagora created the OpenLLM France community, alongside other French Artificial Intelligence companies and organizations. In 2025, the company launched Lucie, an opensource Large Language Model.

explainer.lead: Linagora is a French open-source software editor founded in June 2000 by Alexandre Zapolsky and Michel-Marie Maudet. It matters in the AI ecosystem for creating the OpenLLM France community in 2023 and launching the open-source Large Language Model Lucie in 2025.

tiers.eli5: It is a French software company that builds open-source tools and helps organize other French groups working on open AI models.
tiers.practitioner: Teams working in the French open-source AI ecosystem may encounter Linagora through its community and model initiatives. A pitfall is treating it as only an AI lab: it is primarily an open source software editor with around 200 employees spread across several countries.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition applies; it is an organization. It was founded in June 2000, is located in France plus Belgium, Canada, Vietnam, the United States and Tunisia, and employs around 200 people.

explainer.example: A developer in France could contribute to the OpenLLM France community or use Lucie for French-language NLP tasks.
